newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot hopes to get first Boeing 737s in H1 '97.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot hopes to get first Boeing 737s in H1 '97.

text.p: Aeroflot hopes to get the first two of 10 Boeing 737-400 jets it plans to buy over the next two years in time for the peak summer passenger season next year, a senior company official said on Monday.
Deputy Chief Executive Valery Okulov told Reuters it was still necessary to resolve a few questions about the purchase at the government level.
"I cannot name an exact date when the final agreement will be signed," Okulov said, adding that Boeing was ready to begin assembling aircraft immediately for Aeroflot.
Shaposhnikov said the purchase, which Aeroflot sources said could total $350 million, will be funded by loans and the airline's own funds.
Okulov said all 10 jets would be powered by General Electric Co engines.
He also said Aeroflot Russian International Airlines would soon announce an international tender to design the cabins.
Aeroflot signed a letter of intent to buy 10 jets from Boeing at the Farnborough international air show in Britain earlier this month.
Last Friday Aeroflot chief executive Yevgeny Shaposhnikov told a news conference that the 737s would replace 13 outdated Tupolev-134 jets.
"Aeroflot's losses from operating these aircraft will be $500,000 this year," Shaposhnikov said.

Earlier this month the premier of Russia's autonomous region of Tatarstan denounced Aeroflot's decision to buy Boeing planes in 1997 and 1998, saying it would hurt the crisis-ridden Russian aviation industry.
Russian plane-maker Tupolev is based in the Tatarstan capital of Kazan.
But Shaposhnikov has rejected the criticism, saying the purchase is good for Aeroflot.
Shaposhnikov said Aeroflot could not wait for new Russian-made aircraft, and had chosen the Boeings because there were no Russian competitors in its class.
It plans to carry one million passengers a year with the Boeing jets. Last year it carried a total of 3.5 million passengers.
It operates 18 Russian-made Ilyushin-86, six Ilyushin-96-300 and 27 Ilyushin-62 long-range jets, 29 Tupolev-154 and 13 Tupolev-134 medium-range planes.
It leases two Boeing-767 and 10 Airbus A-310 long-range jets, of which four were added in August.
